premise.text: Seed terms: Time Travel, Ghostwriter, River / Creek, Being recognized, Socially Aware, Gossipy
premise.displayText: A time machine turns Thanksgiving gossip into a cold case with deviled eggs.
premise.headline: A time machine turns Thanksgiving gossip into a cold case with deviled eggs.

jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: First Draft
jokes.joke: I hired a ghostwriter for my memoir, and he used time travel, which sounds efficient until you realize he came back furious about my character arc. He said, “I fixed your ending.” I said, “I’m still alive.” He said, “That was the first draft.”

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: My Time Machine Has a Ghostwriter
jokes.joke: I finally built a time machine, went back to fix my biggest regret: that email I sent my ex at 2 AM. So I go back, stop myself, and past-me says, “relax, I hired a ghostwriter.” Turns out the email was professionally written. That’s the email that ended it. She wasn’t mad I was a mess — she was mad I clearly had help and still chose those words.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Historical Priorities
jokes.joke: People say if they got a time machine, they’d go back and change history. Stop a war, buy stock in Apple. I’m way too gossipy for that kind of pressure. The space-time continuum is fine. I just want to time-travel back to Thanksgiving 1998, hide in the pantry, and finally hear what Uncle Dave said right before Aunt Linda hit him with a deviled egg. You guys can save the world. I just need to know why Dave spent that winter living in a Honda.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Time Traveler Recognized
jokes.joke: Man, being recognized in public is tough enough, but try it as a time traveler. The other night at the bar, this guy walks up and says, “Hey, aren’t you that dude who warned us about the election results last week?” I’m like, “Shhh, I haven’t even gone back yet! Keep it down before I change your future!” Now everyone’s hitting me up for lottery numbers and breakup spoilers. Time travel should come with an NDA, folks.

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: The Creek Celebrity
jokes.joke: I went for a walk by this little creek near my place, just trying to clear my head, when a guy jogs past, squints at me, and goes, “Hey… don’t I know you?” And I’m like, wow, I can’t even be anonymous in nature. Even the ducks looked over like, “Yeah, that’s him… the guy who slipped here last week.”

featureImagePrompt:
Generate one polished web feature image for Paperclipalypse.

ASPECT RATIO: exactly 2:1, horizontal wide banner, target preview size 1024x506.

Style: full-color gothic newspaper-comic illustration, darkly funny but warm, clean black ink, crisp editorial cartoon linework, cinematic stage lighting, high contrast, readable composition. Not monochrome. Not sepia-only. Use a balanced color palette: warm amber stage lights, dark bronze and silver metal paperclip, muted greens and autumn browns for the Thanksgiving scene, dusty blue-gray shadows, cream-white text, and subtle deep red accents.

Composition instructions, not visible labels:
- LEFT: a charming anthropomorphic metallic paperclip stand-up comedian at a vintage microphone on a small stage, expressive and related to the Paperclipalypse paperclip-comedian logo, but not identical.
- CENTER: the winning joke scene as visual comedy action: a glowing homemade time machine near a Thanksgiving dining room, a nosy narrator hiding in a pantry doorway, Uncle Dave reacting, Aunt Linda holding or throwing a deviled egg, and a small visual hint of an old Honda outside or through a window. Keep it energetic, funny, non-gory, and easy to understand.
- RIGHT: a clean dark framed poster panel containing the winning joke text in large cream-white lettering with generous margins and legible line breaks.

Visible text allowed in the entire image: the right-panel joke text, a tiny stage sign reading Paperclipalypse, and optionally a small header above the panel: Winner: Gemini Flash - Historical Priorities.
Do not render layout words, percentages, prompt labels, section names, fake captions, signatures, watermarks, or filler microtext.

Exact joke text to render in the right panel:
People say if they got a time machine, they’d go back and change history. Stop a war, buy stock in Apple. I’m way too gossipy for that kind of pressure. The space-time continuum is fine. I just want to time-travel back to Thanksgiving 1998, hide in the pantry, and finally hear what Uncle Dave said right before Aunt Linda hit him with a deviled egg. You guys can save the world. I just need to know why Dave spent that winter living in a Honda.

Use only this winning joke as the scene source. Do not add river, creek, ghostwriter, or celebrity motifs unless they are in the joke text. The image should be a balanced feature graphic: paperclip comic on left, joke scene in middle, readable text panel on right.

Text rules: use simple clean lettering, spell every word correctly, keep the text inside the right panel, and do not distort letter shapes. The website HTML remains the canonical exact joke text if image lettering is imperfect.

The final image should feel like a finished feature image for an AI comedy tournament: funny, stylish, readable, full-color, and visually balanced.
